rows: A flood alert means flooding is possible and people should prepare.
A flood warning means flooding is expected and people should act.
Severe flood warnings indicate danger to life and require urgent action.
The Environment Agency provides live warning information for England.
Flood alerts are commonly issued two to twelve hours before flooding where possible.
Official advice includes avoiding walking, cycling or driving through flood water.
Businesses and organisations can register locations and contacts for warning messages.
Flood planning should cover documents, medicines, livestock, equipment and safe routes.
Warning status is dynamic and must be read from the live Environment Agency service.
A warning-area intersection does not prove that every parcel inside the area will flood or at the same depth.
MHRA publishes alerts, recalls and safety information for medicines and medical devices.
Alerts can include medicine defect notifications, recalls and field safety notices.
Each alert identifies the affected product or device and the required audience or action.
Organisations should assess whether affected stock or equipment is present.
Recall classes and notices communicate different levels and types of action.
Field safety notices support action on medical-device safety issues.
Subscribers can use email or feed updates to track new notices.
Records provide issue dates and supporting details for audit and response.
An alert does not establish that an affected product is present at a particular premises.
Product, batch, model and date matching are required before any local safety conclusion.
Tuberculosis is a bacterial infection that most commonly affects the lungs but can affect other organs.
Pulmonary or throat TB can spread through the air when an infectious person coughs or sneezes.
A persistent cough, fever, night sweats, reduced appetite and unexplained weight loss can be symptoms.
Early diagnosis and treatment reduce illness and onward transmission.
UKHSA monitors TB trends and publishes surveillance information.
TB is a notifiable disease in England.
Public-health teams support contact tracing and outbreak management.
Prevention work includes awareness, testing, treatment adherence and targeted screening.
Population surveillance trends do not establish transmission at a particular address.
Clinical diagnosis, infectiousness and contact risk require authorised case investigation, not property inference.
RIDDOR requires responsible persons to report specified work-related injuries, diseases and dangerous occurrences.
Responsible persons include employers, some self-employed people and people in control of work premises.
Reportable incidents include defined injuries, occupational diseases and dangerous occurrences.
Reports are generally made through the appropriate HSE online form.
Records must be kept for reportable events and specified over-seven-day injuries.
An incident must be work-related and meet a reporting category to fall within RIDDOR.
Fatal and specified serious incidents have urgent reporting arrangements.
RIDDOR data supports regulator response and occupational safety surveillance.
A recorded or reportable event is an operational incident, not a general safety score for the whole property.
Members of the public or injured workers are not normally the responsible reporter unless they separately hold that legal role.
